extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism adjudication from primary text and local figure panels; automated protein-synthesis/prose locator notes were removed.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: An-cecB shows a membrane-associated antimalarial mechanism: it has low hemolysis on normal erythrocytes but increased hemolysis under cholesterol-depleted or P. falciparum-infected erythrocyte conditions, while An-cecB-1 has minimal infected-RBC hemolysis.
direct_assay_types: P. falciparum schizont-infected erythrocyte hemolysis assay

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:The antimalarial mechanism of An-cecB; xml:fig=5:Fig 5
source_locator.evidence_note: Primary text and Fig. 5 report hemolysis against normal, cholesterol-depleted, and P. falciparum-infected erythrocytes.

mechanism_claims.limitations: The mechanism is supported for the tested in vitro erythrocyte/parasite systems; it should not be generalized to all cecropins or to mosquito-stage activity without additional evidence.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Transmission electron microscopy supports direct parasite structural injury after An-cecB exposure, including parasite shrinkage, membrane disorientation/dissolution, vacuole formation, and disintegration; An-cecB-1 more strongly associates with vacuole formation.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: An-cecB and An-cecB-1 effects on P. falciparum 3D7 parasites

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=8:The antimalarial mechanism of An-cecB; xml:fig=6:Fig 6
source_locator.evidence_note: Primary text and Fig. 6/TEM panel k report abnormal parasite morphology categories after peptide exposure.

mechanism_claims.limitations: TEM morphology supports membrane/structural injury but does not identify a molecular binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: In vivo results separate potency from tolerability: An-cecB is stronger in vitro but weak and toxic in the mouse model, whereas An-cecB-1 retains reduced in vitro potency but better in vivo suppression and lower mammalian-cell toxicity.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=9:Assessment of antimalarial activity against Plasmodium berghei in mice; xml:fig=7:Fig 7
source_locator.evidence_note: Primary text and Fig. 7 report acute oral toxicity and P. berghei four-day suppressive test results.

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is pharmacologic efficacy/toxicity context, not a direct molecular mechanism claim.
